what: My first fix for a replayed record leaving a launched program on another build's code was to never replay a launched unit's record. That kept every no-op `run` out of the no-op lane (unit codegen and the launch link each run), and after other projects were built in the daemon a no-op run of hello walked the whole program again: 12 s.
cost: the warm no-op was 32 ms where 15 was available; one 12 s no-op seen
cause: the record's outputs name the launcher's file, the same bytes for every build, so the record could not say whose code the daemon held; I removed the replay instead of keying it
whys: why wrong: a correctness fix by turning a cache off
why possible: the value under the key (a file) no longer identified the thing that mattered (the code the daemon holds)
why not caught: output checks passed; only timing showed it
why easy: `never` is one line, a key is a design
property: a cached answer whose validity depends on state the key does not name
class: cache turned off instead of keyed: a stale-answer bug fixed by never reusing, where the missing input belongs in the comparison
prevention: rule keys-cover-every-input already says the fix is the key; a review rule for `never replay`/`always rebuild` branches: each names the input the key lacks and why it cannot be added
state: fixed (5226c3d363): replay when the program's held build has the unit's whole record key
